rationale: ROUND 2 on 0b84970d. The gating objection was RIGHT and the defect was fatal, not cosmetic: I gated the whole delivery pipeline on `status='approved'`, and MEASURED 2026-08-25 that value does not exist — 11,983 live rows across 11 statuses (complete/needs_human_review/detected/unresolved/cancelled/deferred/wont_fix/failed/rejected/verified/triaged) and `approved` is not among them. It survives in ONE archive index predicate, which is exactly what made the mistake attractive: the word is in the schema and nothing writes it. The gate could never have opened; delivery would have stalled for ever, silently, looking like 'the owner has not reviewed it yet' — the very failure the absent-row case was designed to avoid, reached through the predicate instead. WHAT THE HANDLER ACTUALLY DOES, read from the code rather than inferred from its name: HandleApproveWorkItem REQUIRES the item at needs_human_review (anything else is a 400) and sets status='complete' with result={'resolution':…,'approved_by':'admin',…}. And 'complete' is necessary but NOT sufficient, because HandleResolveWorkItem writes 'complete' too, with resolved_by. The distinguishing key is approved_by. MEASURED: of 8,003 live complete rows, 155 carry resolved_by and ZERO carry approved_by — the approve path has never run in production, which I now state rather than assume. THE SECOND HIGH WAS ALSO RIGHT, from `guidelines`: site_work_items is a ~7-day rolling window and an approval IS terminal, so 24,990 complete rows already sit in site_work_items_archive. Reading only the live table converted a one-time review into one that EXPIRES after about a week. The gate now UNIONs both tables — the established house pattern for this table (migration 465, 'the promoter reads archived history'), not an invention here. I had a memory note about this exact rolling-window trap and walked into it anyway; that is logged in WRONG_CALLS and the note's trigger has been widened, because it was filed under 'censuses' and I was writing a single-row gate. ALSO ADDED from guardian's low: ReviewItemFiledStatus, because the producer contract has a second silent edge — an item filed at the table's default 'detected' can never be approved at all, so the owner would press the button and get a 400 with delivery blocked and nothing explaining why. Three mutations, all killed. The other objections are answered by checks below rather than by argument.

plan.summary: platform/delivery gains Claim: the one entry point for starting a delivery. It checks the owner's review gate (an approved needs_delivery_review work item), stamps handover idempotently and treats an existing stamp as a refusal, then mints the confirm-transfer token against the handover's own expiry and builds the customer links on the emailed-links host. Links that do not exist yet (ZIP download, Stripe portal) are left EMPTY in the type rather than invented. Config that could build a broken link is refused before the database is touched. No copy, no send, no work-item writing.

edits.rationale: The at-most-once gate, and the ordering IS the design. (1) Review first, so a later bug cannot deliver an unreviewed site. (2) The stamp is the claim: StampHandover is idempotent and reports AlreadyHandedOver, treated as a refusal, so a second call cannot produce a second email however it is retried. This deliberately admits a stamp whose send then failed - loud (the work item fails, a human sees it) rather than silent-and-duplicated (send-then-stamp makes a stamp failure into two emails with no record). (3) Mint last, against the handover's own expiry, so a link cannot outlive the window it belongs to.

THE GATE, CORRECTED. Predicate is now status='complete' AND result ? 'approved_by', read across site_work_items AND site_work_items_archive. Every clause is there because the previous version was wrong: 'approved' is written by nothing (MEASURED, 0 of 11,983 rows); 'complete' alone also matches HandleResolveWorkItem's writes (155 rows carry resolved_by); and omitting the archive makes a terminal approval expire with the ~7-day window (24,990 complete rows are already archived). An absent row in EITHER table still reads as NO, so a producer that forgets to file cannot skip the gate. ReviewItemFiledStatus pins the other half of the producer contract: file at needs_human_review or the approve endpoint 400s.
edits.sketch:
const ReviewItemType = "needs_delivery_review"
const ReviewItemFiledStatus = "needs_human_review"

func Reviewed(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, siteID uuid.UUID) (bool, error) {
	var n int
	err := db.QueryRowContext(ctx, `
		SELECT count(*) FROM (
			SELECT status, result
			  FROM site_work_items
			 WHERE site_id = $1 AND item_type = $2
			UNION ALL
			SELECT status, result
			  FROM site_work_items_archive
			 WHERE site_id = $1 AND item_type = $2
		) z
		WHERE z.status = 'complete'
		  AND z.result ? 'approved_by'
	`, siteID, ReviewItemType).Scan(&n)
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("delivery: read review item: %w", err)
	}
	return n > 0, nil
}

edits.rationale: The email must quote what we ADVERTISE (30 days, the attested fact) and never what we serve (42). Deriving days from Handover.LiveLinkExpiresAt would promise away the slack the owner ruled deliberate on 2026-08-25 - we promise 30 and serve 42 so nobody is cut off on the day they were told. Carrying it on the result means a composer cannot reach for the wrong number without going out of its way.

Each refusal is asserted by what does NOT follow it: an unreviewed site queues no stamp and no mint, an already-delivered site queues no mint, a bad config queues no query at all. THE FOURTH MUTATION PASSED FIRST TIME and that is the finding worth recording: with validate() deleted, Claim ran on to the gate query, sqlmock refused a call it was never told to expect, and the test saw an error and was satisfied - and ExpectationsWereMet does not catch it either, because there were no expectations to meet. A bare 'err != nil' could not distinguish config rejection from a database failure. The test now identifies the error AS the config refusal, and the mutation kills it.

THE SINGLE-USE DECISION, and its dead predecessor: DECISION_2026-08-21b §4 required the confirm token NOT be single-use because /c/ was then a GET that mutated, so a mail scanner's prefetch would spend it and lock the customer out. It stays not-single-use for a reason that outlives the original: the stamp is COALESCEd so a second confirmation cannot move the recorded date, and a customer who clicks twice should get the same answer rather than 'no longer active'. Nothing is protected by spending it. Recorded in the code as a comment naming both the retired and the current reason.

THE GATING DEFECT, MEASURED 2026-08-25: `SELECT status, count(*) FROM site_work_items GROUP BY 1` returns complete 8003 | needs_human_review 962 | detected 803 | unresolved 737 | cancelled 737 | deferred 315 | wont_fix 217 | failed 188 | rejected 9 | verified 9 | triaged 3. NO `approved`. The archive returns complete 24990 | failed 858 | wont_fix 433.

WHAT THE APPROVE HANDLER WRITES, read at internal/core-manager/admin/site_admin_handlers.go (HandleApproveWorkItem, from line 1028): it rejects any item not at needs_human_review with 'item status is %s, expected needs_human_review', then `UPDATE site_work_items SET status = 'complete', completed_at = NOW(), result = jsonb_build_object('resolution', $2, 'approved_by', 'admin', 'follow_on_item', $3)`. HandleResolveWorkItem writes the same status with `jsonb_build_object('resolution', $2, 'resolved_by', 'admin')`, which is why approved_by and not complete is the discriminator.

THE DISCRIMINATOR CHECKED AGAINST LIVE DATA, 2026-08-25: of 8,003 complete rows, 7,848 carry neither key, 155 carry resolved_by, and ZERO carry approved_by. So the approve path has never been exercised in production and the first delivery must drive it deliberately.

THE ARCHIVE, and that reading both is house style not invention: site_work_items_archive carries site_id, item_type, status and result (jsonb), so the UNION is a like-for-like read; migration 465 is literally titled 'promoter reads archived history' and builds the same UNION ALL pair, and the 471 remedy's census does too.

bug_historian asked whether StampHandover's idempotency is schema-enforced or check-then-act. Read at platform/delivery/handover.go:159-182 — it is ONE statement, `UPDATE sites SET handed_over_at = COALESCE(handed_over_at, $2), live_link_expires_at = COALESCE(live_link_expires_at, $3) WHERE id = $1 RETURNING …, handed_over_at <> $2`. No read-then-write, so there is no window; AlreadyHandedOver comes back from the same statement that did (or did not) write.
